title: Extraction of Δ4 Steroids from Tooth Dentin for LC-MS/MS
author: Michael Cherney
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.21203/rs.3.pex-1898/v1
materials: For double blank, add 400 μl water.
Wait 10 minutes to allow passive gravity elution.
Move vials with eluted MTBE to vacuum concentrator.

steps.title: Label centrifuge tubes
steps.instruction: Label a centrifuge tube for each sample and at least three process blanks.

steps.title: Add beads and record weight
steps.instruction: Add approximately 300 mg Lysing Matrix D beads to each tube and record the weight of tube plus beads.

steps.title: Add dentin powder and weigh
steps.instruction: Add 20–100 mg dentin powder to each tube and reweigh to calculate the exact sample mass.

steps.title: Add methanol and internal standard
steps.instruction: Add 1500 µL methanol and 100 µL internal standard (deuterated analytes in 40 % MeOH) to each tube.

steps.title: Vortex and place on rotator
steps.instruction: Vortex each tube for 60 seconds at 10 krpm, then place the tube in a rotator.

steps.title: Rotate extraction mixture
steps.instruction: Rotate the tubes at 30 rpm for 2 hours at 4 °C.

steps.title: Centrifuge extraction tubes
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tubes for 8 minutes at 14 000 g.

steps.title: Transfer supernatant to vials
steps.instruction: Transfer 1350 µL of supernatant from each tube to a labeled autosampler vial; optionally split into two vials for a backup sample (each will contain half the extracted analyte).

steps.title: Evaporate to <50 µL
steps.instruction: Evaporate samples in a vacuum concentrator to less than 50 µL (90–120 minutes, 5.1 torr, ambient temperature).

steps.title: Add clean solvent and water
steps.instruction: Add 40 µL clean methanol and 300 µL water to each vial.

steps.title: Reconstitute by vortexing
steps.instruction: Cap the vials and vortex for 20 seconds at 10 krpm to reconstitute.

steps.title: Pre‑cool concentrator rotor
steps.instruction: Pre‑cool the vacuum‑concentrator rotor at –20 °C for 3 hours (optional if the unit has built‑in refrigeration).

steps.title: Label control and blank vials
steps.instruction: Label autosampler vials for each desired control sample, one SLE process blank, and one double blank.

steps.title: Prepare control sample vials
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL control sample, 100 µL internal standard, and 200 µL water to each control vial.

steps.title: Prepare SLE blank vials
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL internal standard and 300 µL water to each SLE process‑blank vial.

steps.title: Label final analysis vials
steps.instruction: Label autosampler vials for each sample, process blank, and control sample (for LC‑MS/MS).

steps.title: Load vials and SLE columns
steps.instruction: Load the labeled vials and SLE columns into a positive‑pressure manifold.

steps.title: Load samples onto SLE columns
steps.instruction: Pipette each reconstituted sample, control sample, and blank into its designated SLE column.

steps.title: Apply initial pressure to load
steps.instruction: Apply 0.5–3.0 psi N₂ pressure for about 5 seconds to load the sample into the column.

steps.title: Add MTBE extraction solvent
steps.instruction: Add 1800 µL methyl tert‑butyl ether (MTBE) to each column.

steps.title: Apply secondary pressure
steps.instruction: Apply 0.5–1.0 psi N₂ pressure for 5 seconds.

steps.title: Blow columns dry incrementally
steps.instruction: Blow columns dry by applying pressure sequentially: 0.5 psi, 3 psi, 6 psi, and 9 psi, each for 10 seconds.

steps.title: Evaporate to dryness
steps.instruction: Evaporate samples to dryness in the vacuum concentrator with the precooled rotor (20–30 minutes, 5.1 torr, ambient temperature).

steps.title: Place vials on ice
steps.instruction: Remove vials from the concentrator and keep them on ice until reconstitution.

steps.title: Reconstitute final extracts
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL 40 % methanol to each vial, cap, and vortex for 20 seconds at 10 krpm.

steps.title: Store extracts for analysis
steps.instruction: Store the vials in a freezer until LC‑MS/MS analysis.
